To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphorylation of the 19-kDa regulatory light chain of smooth myosin plays an important role in facilitating thick filament reassembly in intact muscle after mechanical perturbation and that this phosphorylation is cyclically associated with repeated muscle stimulation.
MLC phosphorylation facilitates in vitro thick filament reassembly and that the in vivo thick filament density is decreased by mechanical perturbation but is restored by repeated MLC phosphorylation.
MLC phosphorylation facilitates in vitro myosin filament assembly and that MLC phosphorylated during repeated muscle stimulation facilitates in vivo myofibril reassembly after mechanical stress
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MLC kinase activity in thick filament formation and reformation in intact smooth muscle.
how the contractile apparatus responds to mechanical perturbations in vivo.
the mechanism by which myosin filaments in the intact muscle are disassembled and reassembled.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MLC kinase activity is necessary to maintain the thick filament density in intact muscle.
the phosphorylated MLC is required for filament reformation in intact smooth muscle.
phosphorylation of MLC is not essential for the initial assembly of thick filaments in smooth muscle but is required for reassembly of the filamnets after mechanical perturbation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MLC phosphorylation is not necessary for the initial assembly of thick filaments in vivo but is necessary for thick filament reassembly following mechanical perturbation.

the cyclic MLC kinase activity is necessary for the maintenance of the thick filament structure in intact muscle, and the cyclic MLC dephosphorylation is required for the filament dissolution in response to mechanical perturbation.
the phosphorylation of MLC is necessary for the maintenance and reassembly of thick filaments in smooth muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in smooth muscle, MLC phosphorylation facilitates thick filament assembly after mechanical perturbation, and the phosphorylation cycle is required for the maintenance of the thick filament assembly in vivo.
the MLC kinase activity is required to facilitate thick filament reassembly, but the kinase activity is not required to initiate thick filament reassembly.
MLC phosphorylation is not required for thick filament formation in vivo but is required for the reassembly of thick filaments after mechanical perturbation.
